label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 8, samples with blocking 77

report.summary: Transfers show 15.9% 500s and multi-second tail latency while sessions block on a lock held by an idle-in-transaction session. Outbox delivery and pool exhaustion look healthy.

findings.claim: Transfers have 119 HTTP 500s (ratio 0.159) and p95 2.4 s / p99 4.4 s.
findings.reason: Request metrics are COMPLETE and show both failures and slow tail latency in the window.

findings.claim: ledger_app sessions were blocked, waiting on session 62321 (idle in transaction), with waits up to 1.78 s.
findings.reason: Historical blocker samples show three blocked sessions repeatedly waiting on one idle-in-transaction session from 05:45:37 to 05:48:45.

findings.claim: The lock contention plausibly explains the slow and failing transfers. The pool is not exhausted, so the waits come from locks.
findings.reason: Pool timeouts are 0, pending is 0 and acquire time is under 7 ms, so the delay is not pool starvation. The blocking overlaps the symptom window.

findings.claim: The outbox consumer path is healthy. Deliveries all succeeded in about 71 ms and arrivals match publications.
findings.reason: 620 successes, 0 errors and arrivals minus publications of -1. The failed count of 826 is constant, so those failures are old and not new in this window.

limitations: Blocker sampling is every 2 s, so shorter blocks can be missed. There is no per-request link between 500s and blocked sessions.
The statement the idle-in-transaction session 62321 is running, and who owns it, are unknown, so the root cause of the held lock is not identified.
next_checks: Inspect session 62321 (query, transaction start, application name) and what locks it holds on the transfer tables.
Correlate the timing of the 500 responses with the application error logs and lock-wait timeouts.

alternatives.reason: No error logs or per-request traces tie the 500s to the lock waits.
alternatives.hypothesis: The 500s have a different cause, such as an application error or validation path, unrelated to the blocking.

alternatives.reason: Deliveries are fast and all succeed, and the outbox arrives and publishes in step.
alternatives.hypothesis: Outbox delivery or consumer slowness causes the delays.

A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 77 samples
